# Installed local capture 0.6.11

The fixture records the archive from the installer release tag after verifying its length, SHA-256 and production dependency pins. The offline qualification installs it with package scripts disabled. It runs each native hook in an isolated home with synthetic JSONL transcripts and an empty credential environment. A synthetic Linux executable named Codex gives the hook real process ancestry and a private, identity-bound format verdict. Its descendants exit with the observed hook status. The instrumentation records the internal hook outcome and child acknowledgement and trips on provider dispatch or model-port invocation.

The exchanges include Claude Code SessionStart, Stop and PreCompact, and Codex SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop and PreCompact. They cover append, repeat, incomplete transcript and stdin, event mismatch, a Codex fork, scoped pause and disable, and operator deletion followed by fresh hook processes on the original transcript. Cursor positions are bytes and ordinals count selected messages. The archive column records each visible saved Raw part and its source time. The installed delete completed and removed the conversation from Raw listings. The synthetic sentinel was still present in the closed installed SQLite file after restart and replay. Candidate deletion qualification requires the closed candidate file to omit it.

## Normalization

- The four fixture input variables `$node`, `$hook`, `$installation` and `$transcript` materialize to absolute paths. The harness checks the native command against the full installed argv, including both environment exclusions and the 160-second timeout. Input JSON field order and spelling are literal.
- The replay uses Node's experimental warning flag for identical hook conditions across the two Node versions, then checks exact exit status, stdout and stderr. The preload observes the internal hook and transport exchange separately from the public output.
- The setup fixture seeds its synthetic store and installation identities so Codex's derived message IDs replay literally. Hook processes generate conversation IDs normally. Generated conversation UUIDs are checked as v4 UUIDs and assigned numbered markers in first-observed order. Reuse preserves equality. Synthetic session and source message IDs remain literal. If a cursor contains a pending timestamp, the harness checks its integer shape and clock bound before replacing it. Source times, cursor offsets and ordinals remain literal.
- Cursor progress projects the offset, issued ordinal, selection state, refusal reason and pending retry metadata. Private HMAC state and device/inode evidence are outside that projection. The child acknowledgement retains all parsed fields apart from the validated UUID markers.

Run the installed replay with `node tools/testing/local-capture-wire.qualification.mjs --baseline`. Run the packaged replay with `--candidate`. Exit 77 identifies the current provider-free Core capture gate. The replay also checks that changing an observed reply causes the installed comparison to fail.
